A write-ahead log is a file that stores records of all changes made to the database before they are made to the database itself. If the system crashes before these records are written to the database, the database can recover by using the records in the write-ahead log to undo any changes that were applied. This process is called recovery.

After the system crashes, the database will go through a process called recovery. During recovery, the database will read through the write-ahead log and apply any changes that were not yet written to the database. However, it will also undo any changes that were applied just before the crash, up until the point where the system crashed. This ensures that the database is left in a consistent state, even if the system crashed just as a transaction was being applied.

A write-ahead log is particularly useful for databases that support transactions, which are groups of operations that are treated as a single unit of work. If a transaction is in progress when the system crashes, the database can recover by rolling back the entire transaction, ensuring that the database is left in a consistent state.
